what: Alnylam pioneered RNA interference medicines, which silence the genes that produce harmful proteins. Its medicines treat rare inherited diseases, and Amvuttra has been approved for the much larger ATTR amyloidosis cardiomyopathy market.
customers: Specialists treating amyloidosis and rare genetic disease, with treatment paid for by insurers and health systems.
money: treatments for ATTR amyloidosis, now including heart involvement
rare disease medicines and partnered royalties
moat: A delivery technology that gets RNA medicines into liver cells reliably, built over two decades, with patents and a prescriber base in diseases few companies work on.
risks: Competing ATTR medicines from much larger companies are launching into the same market
Operating margin of 14% is thin while it funds a large pipeline
The shares price in a very successful cardiomyopathy launch
opportunities: Revenue grew about 65% last year and about 53% a year over three years
The ATTR cardiomyopathy market is far larger than the rare disease base it started from
Cash of about $3.6 billion against $900 million of debt
watch: Amvuttra prescriptions in cardiomyopathy and share against competing treatments.
